key_insight: PROUD reduces forgetting in multimodal continual instruction tuning by optimizing a compact update subspace in the vision–language projector’s final linear layer.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support sequential adaptation of engineering vision–language assistants with low training overhead, but solid-mechanics applications are not evaluated in the abstract.
method: Combine retained input statistics and initial task gradients to select a metric-orthonormal subspace balancing task gain against interface drift.
Train within the fixed subspace using an exact Frobenius penalty to constrain drift.
Losslessly merge updates into the projector with no added inference or routing overhead.
evidence_signal: On UCIT and CoIN across multiple MLLM backbones, the abstract reports higher continual accuracy and less forgetting than recent replay-free baselines, using a fraction of their trainable parameters.
watch_item: A subspace fixed at task onset may become less aligned with useful update directions as training progresses; the abstract provides no quantitative sensitivity analysis.
paper_title: Projector Subspace Optimization for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
